newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 97 winter wheat crop seen well below 96 - LTO.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 97 winter wheat crop seen well below 96 - LTO.

text.p: The Dutch winter wheat harvest this year looks to be down by at least 10 percent on 1996's 1.22 million tonnes, the Dutch farmers' body LTO said on Tuesday.

Initial indications from the south of the country showed a per hectare yield between 15 and 20 percent below last year's 9.1 tonnes, but there were signs the rest of the country had fared slightly better, LTO spokesman Jack Luiten told Reuters.

"Overall the crop will be at least 10 percent below last year's. In the south, the crop is worse but that accounts for only 25 to 30 percent of the Dutch total," he said. "In around two weeks time, we'll have the whole crop in."
In 1996 the country harvested a record 1.22 million tonnes of winter wheat from 135,000 hectares.

He said the crop in the south had been affected by mould and by a relatively short harvest period. "The time the crop was ripe for harvesting was very short, and that has affected it compared to last year," he said.
"But it could be different in the middle and the north of the country. We'll have more details in a couple of weeks."
